newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican opposition forms bloc to outvote ruling party.
newsitem.headline: Mexican opposition forms bloc to outvote ruling party.

text.p: Mexican opposition parties have formed a bloc that could outvote the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in the lower house of congress, Mexican media reported on Tuesday.
"They have formed an opposition bloc to avoid that the PRI is the only party that takes decisions (in congress)," TV network Televisa anchorman Guillermo Ortega said.

In historic July 6 elections, the PRI lost a key element of its 68-year grip on power by losing its absolute majority in the Chamber of Deputies. The PRI only won 239 seats of the 500 in the lower house.

Leaders of four opposition parties, including the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) and the conservative National Action Party (PAN), met on Monday in Mexico City to work out a strategy to break the PRI's grip on power.
The PRD and PAN, together with the Mexican Greens Party (PVEM) and the Workers' Party (PT), have a combined total of 261 votes.
"There is going to be no PRI majority," Jorge Emilio Gonzalez Martinez of the Mexican Greens Party told radio network Radio Red, speaking about the opposition bloc.
Gonzalez Martinez played down the possibility of outvoting the PRI, insisting that the four opposition parties and the PRI would all form part of the lower house's governing commission.

But he did admit that for the first time in Mexico's modern history an opposition congressman could be the leader of the house, through which most major bills have to pass, including the federal budget.

The opposition parties also agreed not to negotiate on a unilateral basis with the PRI and they called the ruling party to PRI to recognise the new political front and agree to work with the bloc, he added.
The PRI's first reaction was to shun the opposition move. PRI spokesman Oscar Gonzalez branded the pact as "inconvenient, exclusionist and with shades of revenge."

PRI congressman-elect Mariano Palacios Alcocer told the daily Reforma that the PRI would not negotiate and added that the opposition bloc was not healthy for the democratic processes at work in the country.
